canonical_objects: head noun number read at an auxiliary with have/has
a number behaviour whose vocabulary is disjoint from the was/were family
the token control for the shared number direction
decision_changed: This decides whether the shared number direction is a NUMBER feature or a was/were token axis. Registered in advance, both branches: transfer against the was/were family >= 0.50 means the direction survives a vocabulary change and the shared-number reading stands; <= 0.20 means the earlier 1.053 and 0.600 were a token axis and the shared-number claim is RETRACTED; between is INCONCLUSIVE and is not resolved by raising rank. If the screen returns a one-sided capability failure -- plausible here, since the durative adjunct must actually select the perfect -- the registered stop rule is ONE repair of the weak side, per ops/README.md.
matched_prior_claims: circuits/followups/das_quantifier_override_transfer_v1_result.json and das_matched_slot_number_transfer_v1_result.json report one rank-1 direction shared by three number behaviours at a matched auxiliary slot, transfers 1.053 and 0.600.
All three of those behaviours answer with the IDENTICAL pair ' was' / ' were', so a direction separating those two tokens would produce the same transfers with no shared number feature.

circuits/followups/das_slot_confound_calibration_v1_result.json showed the one available disjoint-vocabulary comparison (possessive their/his) also differs in read slot, and a slot difference alone collapses transfer from 1.053 to 0.067, so it could not discriminate.
novelty_delta: Thirty-fourth behaviour, authored as a control on my own result rather than for breadth. It is the first number behaviour in the corpus that holds the READ SLOT fixed against the was/were family while changing the ANSWER TOKENS: a fronted durative adjunct selects the perfect, so the same head-noun number is read at an auxiliary in the same position, answering ' have' / ' has'. Matched slot with disjoint vocabulary is the one configuration in which a transfer is interpretable as evidence about number rather than about tokens, and no existing pair in this corpus has it.
reviewer: Claude ops lane, testing a token confound in its own strongest result
